translation_en: Heaven and earth, dark and yellow; the cosmos, vast and desolate. Sun and moon, waxing and waning; stars and constellations, spread and arrayed. Cold comes, heat goes; autumn harvests, winter stores. Intercalary months complete the year; musical pitches harmonize with yang. Clouds rise to bring rain; dew condenses into frost. Gold is born in beautiful waters; jade comes from Kungang. The sword called Juque; the pearl known as Night-Shining. Precious fruits: plums and crabapples; important vegetables: mustard and ginger. The sea is salty, rivers are fresh; fish dive, birds soar. Dragon Master, Fire Emperor; Bird Official, Human Sovereign. They began creating writing; then came clothing and garments. Yielding the throne, ceding the state: Yu and Tang of the line of Tao. Comforting the people, punishing the guilty: King Fa of Zhou, King Tang of Yin. Sitting in court, inquiring of the Way; ruling effortlessly, bringing order. Lovingly nurturing the common people; subjects submitting, even the Rong and Qiang. Far and near, one body; all guests return to the king. Phoenixes sing in the bamboo; white colts graze in the meadow. Transformation covers the grasses and trees; its blessings reach all directions. This body and its hair come from the four elements and five constants. Respectfully cherish your upbringing; dare not damage or injure. Women admire chastity and purity; men emulate talent and virtue. Know your faults and always correct them; gain ability and never forget it. Do not speak of others' shortcomings; do not rely on your own strengths. Trustworthiness should be verifiable; one's capacity is hard to measure. Mo Zi grieved over dyed silk; the Odes praised the lambskin. Emulate virtuous conduct; strive to be a sage in thought. Build virtue, establish a name; keep form upright, appearance correct. An empty valley carries sound; a vacant hall echoes. Disaster comes from accumulated evil; fortune follows from doing good. A foot of jade is not the treasure; an inch of time is what to compete for. Serve your father, serve your lord, with strictness and respect. In filial piety, exhaust your strength; in loyalty, devote your life. Treading on thin ice over deep water; rising early, keeping parents warm and cool. Like orchids in fragrance; like pines in flourishing. Rivers flow without ceasing; deep pools reflect clearly. In demeanor, appear thoughtful; in speech, be calm and steady. Be sincere and fine at the start; be careful and proper at the end. The foundation of glory and enterprise; its basis is vast beyond measure. When learning excels, enter government service; hold office and join in governance. Preserve like the sweet pear tree; depart and be praised even more. Joy differs between noble and humble; rites distinguish high and low. Above harmonious, below respectful; husband leads, wife follows. Outside, receive the tutor's instruction; inside, follow the mother's example. All the aunts, uncles, and elders; treat nephews and nieces as your own children. Brothers share deep bonds; of one breath, connected branches. In friendship, share commitments; polish and admonish each other. Benevolence, compassion, and sympathy; never depart from these, even in haste. Integrity, righteousness, modesty, and deference; never diminish these, even in hardship. When nature is calm, emotions are at ease; when the heart stirs, the spirit tires. Hold to truth and your will is full; chase things and your purpose shifts. Firmly maintain refined conduct; good rank will come of itself. The great cities of China; the two capitals, East and West. Backed by Mang, facing Luo; floating on the Wei, set upon the Jing. Palaces rise in lush splendor; towers and pavilions soar startlingly. Paintings depict birds and beasts; colors portray immortals and spirits. Side chambers open beside; curtained halls face the pillars. Banquets are spread with mats; drums, zithers, and reed organs play. Ascending the steps to the throne; caps turn like revolving stars. Right passage to the inner quarters; left leads to the Hall of Light. Classics and canons are gathered; talented scholars are assembled. Du Cao's drafts, Zhong's clerical script; lacquered writings, wall sutras. Officials arrayed: generals and ministers; flanking the lanes, ministers by the scholar trees. Households enfeoffed in eight counties; families supplied with a thousand soldiers. Tall caps accompany the imperial chariot; carriages surge, tassels flutter. Hereditary wealth and luxury; carriages sleek, horses light. Meritorious deeds richly recorded; inscribed on steles and carved in stone. Pan Xi and Yi Yin; aiding their times, the Grand Steward. Dwelling at Qufu; who but Dan could have built it? Duke Huan united and corrected; aiding the weak, supporting the faltering. Qi turned back the Han and the Hui; Yue's persuasion moved King Wu Ding. Outstanding talents served diligently; many scholars brought genuine peace. Jin and Chu competed for supremacy; Zhao and Wei were hemmed in. Borrowing a road to destroy Guo; treading the soil at the covenant assembly. He Zun upheld the law; Han's legacy burdened by harsh punishment. Qi Jian, Po, and Mu; their military use was the most brilliant. Proclaiming might across the desert; fame racing through painted history. The nine provinces bear Yu's traces; a hundred commanderies under Qin's union. The sacred peak Mount Tai; the altar of Zen at Cloud Pavilion. Wild Goose Gate, the Purple Pass; Cock Field, the Red Walls. Kunming Pool, Jieshi Rock; the Great Wilds, Dongting Lake. Vast and far, stretching endlessly; cliffs and peaks, dark and deep. Governance is rooted in agriculture; attend to planting and harvesting. Begin plowing the southern fields; I plant millet and grain. When taxes are ripe, offer the new harvest; encourage with rewards, demote and promote. Mencius valued simplicity; Shi Yu held to uprightness. Strive for the Mean; be diligent, humble, and careful. Listen to sounds, examine principles; observe appearance, discern character. Bequeath excellent plans; encourage earnest cultivation. Examine yourself with admonition; favor and excess lead to extremes. Disgrace and humiliation draw near shame; the forest and marsh are fortunate retreats. The two Shu perceived the moment; who compelled them to resign? Dwell in solitude, abide in leisure; in silence and stillness. Seek the ancients, explore their words; scatter worries, wander carefree. Joyful melodies dispel sorrow; sorrows depart, happiness beckons. Lotus channels, water lilies; gardens overgrown, tendrils reaching. Loquats green in late season; parasol trees wither early. Old roots hidden in shadow; fallen leaves drift and sway. The great fish swims alone; soaring, brushing the crimson sky. Lost in reading at the market; eyes fixed on the book satchel. Easy and light are what we fear; walls have ears. Prepare meals and serve food; suit the palate, fill the belly. When sated, cook and slaughter; when hungry, even dregs and husks suffice. Relatives and old friends; old and young get different fare. Concubines spin and weave; attendants serve in chambers. Round fans of fine silk; silver candles gleaming bright. Daytime sleep, evening slumber; blue bamboo mats, ivory beds. String songs and wine banquets; raising cups and lifting goblets. Clapping hands and stamping feet; in joy and ease and health. Legitimate heirs carry on the line; sacrificial rites of winter and autumn. Kowtow and bow again; with awe, fear, and trepidation. Letters and documents should be concise; replies should be thorough. When the body is dirty, think of bathing; when hot, wish for coolness. Donkeys, mules, calves, and bulls; startled, they leap and prance. Execute and behead thieves and bandits; capture and seize rebels and fugitives. Bu Yi's archery, Liao Wan's ball play; Ji Kang's zither, Ruan Ji's whistling. Tian's brush, Lun's paper; Jun's ingenuity, Ren's fishing. Release disputes for common benefit; all are fine and wonderful. Mao Qiang and Xi Shi's beauty; artful frowns, lovely smiles. Years fly like arrows, always pressing; the sun's glow shines brightly. The celestial armillary sphere revolves; the dark moon's phases cycle in light. Point to the firewood to prolong blessings; forever peaceful, auspicious, and good. Measured steps, leading the way; looking up and down in the corridors of state. Bound sashes, dignified and solemn; lingering, gazing afar. Lonely and ignorant, few in learning; foolish and benighted, subject to ridicule. These are the grammatical particles: yan, zai, hu, ye.

Gold is born in beautiful waters; jade comes from Kungang. The sword called Juque; the pearl known as Night-Shining. Precious fruits: plums and crabapples; important vegetables: mustard and ginger. The sea is salty, rivers are fresh; fish dive, birds soar. Dragon Master, Fire Emperor; Bird Official, Human Sovereign. They began creating writing; then came clothing and garments. Yielding the throne, ceding the state: Yu and Tang of the line of Tao. Comforting the people, punishing the guilty: King Fa of Zhou, King Tang of Yin. Sitting in court, inquiring of the Way; ruling effortlessly, bringing order. Lovingly nurturing the common people; subjects submitting, even the Rong and Qiang. Far and near, one body; all guests return to the king. Phoenixes sing in the bamboo; white colts graze in the meadow. Transformation covers the grasses and trees; its blessings reach all directions. This body and its hair come from the four elements and five constants. Respectfully cherish your upbringing; dare not damage or injure. Women admire chastity and purity; men emulate talent and virtue. Know your faults and always correct them; gain ability and never forget it. Do not speak of others' shortcomings; do not rely on your own strengths. Trustworthiness should be verifiable; one's capacity is hard to measure. Mo Zi grieved over dyed silk; the Odes praised the lambskin. Emulate virtuous conduct; strive to be a sage in thought. Build virtue, establish a name; keep form upright, appearance correct. An empty valley carries sound; a vacant hall echoes. Disaster comes from accumulated evil; fortune follows from doing good. A foot of jade is not the treasure; an inch of time is what to compete for. Serve your father, serve your lord, with strictness and respect. In filial piety, exhaust your strength; in loyalty, devote your life. Treading on thin ice over deep water; rising early, keeping parents warm and cool. Like orchids in fragrance; like pines in flourishing. Rivers flow without ceasing; deep pools reflect clearly. In demeanor, appear thoughtful; in speech, be calm and steady. Be sincere and fine at the start; be careful and proper at the end. The foundation of glory and enterprise; its basis is vast beyond measure. When learning excels, enter government service; hold office and join in governance. Preserve like the sweet pear tree; depart and be praised even more. Joy differs between noble and humble; rites distinguish high and low. Above harmonious, below respectful; husband leads, wife follows. Outside, receive the tutor's instruction; inside, follow the mother's example. All the aunts, uncles, and elders; treat nephews and nieces as your own children. Brothers share deep bonds; of one breath, connected branches. In friendship, share commitments; polish and admonish each other. Benevolence, compassion, and sympathy; never depart from these, even in haste. Integrity, righteousness, modesty, and deference; never diminish these, even in hardship. When nature is calm, emotions are at ease; when the heart stirs, the spirit tires. Hold to truth and your will is full; chase things and your purpose shifts. Firmly maintain refined conduct; good rank will come of itself. The great cities of China; the two capitals, East and West. Backed by Mang, facing Luo; floating on the Wei, set upon the Jing. Palaces rise in lush splendor; towers and pavilions soar startlingly. Paintings depict birds and beasts; colors portray immortals and spirits. Side chambers open beside; curtained halls face the pillars. Banquets are spread with mats; drums, zithers, and reed organs play. Ascending the steps to the throne; caps turn like revolving stars. Right passage to the inner quarters; left leads to the Hall of Light. Classics and canons are gathered; talented scholars are assembled. Du Cao's drafts, Zhong's clerical script; lacquered writings, wall sutras. Officials arrayed: generals and ministers; flanking the lanes, ministers by the scholar trees. Households enfeoffed in eight counties; families supplied with a thousand soldiers. Tall caps accompany the imperial chariot; carriages surge, tassels flutter. Hereditary wealth and luxury; carriages sleek, horses light. Meritorious deeds richly recorded; inscribed on steles and carved in stone. Pan Xi and Yi Yin; aiding their times, the Grand Steward. Dwelling at Qufu; who but Dan could have built it? Duke Huan united and corrected; aiding the weak, supporting the faltering. Qi turned back the Han and the Hui; Yue's persuasion moved King Wu Ding. Outstanding talents served diligently; many scholars brought genuine peace. Jin and Chu competed for supremacy; Zhao and Wei were hemmed in. Borrowing a road to destroy Guo; treading the soil at the covenant assembly. He Zun upheld the law; Han's legacy burdened by harsh punishment. Qi Jian, Po, and Mu; their military use was the most brilliant. Proclaiming might across the desert; fame racing through painted history. The nine provinces bear Yu's traces; a hundred commanderies under Qin's union. The sacred peak Mount Tai; the altar of Zen at Cloud Pavilion. Wild Goose Gate, the Purple Pass; Cock Field, the Red Walls. Kunming Pool, Jieshi Rock; the Great Wilds, Dongting Lake. Vast and far, stretching endlessly; cliffs and peaks, dark and deep. Governance is rooted in agriculture; attend to planting and harvesting. Begin plowing the southern fields; I plant millet and grain. When taxes are ripe, offer the new harvest; encourage with rewards, demote and promote. Mencius valued simplicity; Shi Yu held to uprightness. Strive for the Mean; be diligent, humble, and careful. Listen to sounds, examine principles; observe appearance, discern character. Bequeath excellent plans; encourage earnest cultivation. Examine yourself with admonition; favor and excess lead to extremes. Disgrace and humiliation draw near shame; the forest and marsh are fortunate retreats. The two Shu perceived the moment; who compelled them to resign? Dwell in solitude, abide in leisure; in silence and stillness. Seek the ancients, explore their words; scatter worries, wander carefree. Joyful melodies dispel sorrow; sorrows depart, happiness beckons. Lotus channels, water lilies; gardens overgrown, tendrils reaching. Loquats green in late season; parasol trees wither early. Old roots hidden in shadow; fallen leaves drift and sway. The great fish swims alone; soaring, brushing the crimson sky. Lost in reading at the market; eyes fixed on the book satchel. Easy and light are what we fear; walls have ears. Prepare meals and serve food; suit the palate, fill the belly. When sated, cook and slaughter; when hungry, even dregs and husks suffice. Relatives and old friends; old and young get different fare. Concubines spin and weave; attendants serve in chambers. Round fans of fine silk; silver candles gleaming bright. Daytime sleep, evening slumber; blue bamboo mats, ivory beds. String songs and wine banquets; raising cups and lifting goblets. Clapping hands and stamping feet; in joy and ease and health. Legitimate heirs carry on the line; sacrificial rites of winter and autumn. Kowtow and bow again; with awe, fear, and trepidation. Letters and documents should be concise; replies should be thorough. When the body is dirty, think of bathing; when hot, wish for coolness. Donkeys, mules, calves, and bulls; startled, they leap and prance. Execute and behead thieves and bandits; capture and seize rebels and fugitives. Bu Yi's archery, Liao Wan's ball play; Ji Kang's zither, Ruan Ji's whistling. Tian's brush, Lun's paper; Jun's ingenuity, Ren's fishing. Release disputes for common benefit; all are fine and wonderful. Mao Qiang and Xi Shi's beauty; artful frowns, lovely smiles. Years fly like arrows, always pressing; the sun's glow shines brightly. The celestial armillary sphere revolves; the dark moon's phases cycle in light. Point to the firewood to prolong blessings; forever peaceful, auspicious, and good. Measured steps, leading the way; looking up and down in the corridors of state. Bound sashes, dignified and solemn; lingering, gazing afar. Lonely and ignorant, few in learning; foolish and benighted, subject to ridicule. These are the grammatical particles: yan, zai, hu, ye.

Gold is born in beautiful waters; jade comes from Kungang. The sword called Juque; the pearl known as Night-Shining. Precious fruits: plums and crabapples; important vegetables: mustard and ginger. The sea is salty, rivers are fresh; fish dive, birds soar. Dragon Master, Fire Emperor; Bird Official, Human Sovereign. They began creating writing; then came clothing and garments. Yielding the throne, ceding the state: Yu and Tang of the line of Tao. Comforting the people, punishing the guilty: King Fa of Zhou, King Tang of Yin. Sitting in court, inquiring of the Way; ruling effortlessly, bringing order. Lovingly nurturing the common people; subjects submitting, even the Rong and Qiang. Far and near, one body; all guests return to the king. Phoenixes sing in the bamboo; white colts graze in the meadow. Transformation covers the grasses and trees; its blessings reach all directions. This body and its hair come from the four elements and five constants. Respectfully cherish your upbringing; dare not damage or injure. Women admire chastity and purity; men emulate talent and virtue. Know your faults and always correct them; gain ability and never forget it. Do not speak of others' shortcomings; do not rely on your own strengths. Trustworthiness should be verifiable; one's capacity is hard to measure. Mo Zi grieved over dyed silk; the Odes praised the lambskin. Emulate virtuous conduct; strive to be a sage in thought. Build virtue, establish a name; keep form upright, appearance correct. An empty valley carries sound; a vacant hall echoes. Disaster comes from accumulated evil; fortune follows from doing good. A foot of jade is not the treasure; an inch of time is what to compete for. Serve your father, serve your lord, with strictness and respect. In filial piety, exhaust your strength; in loyalty, devote your life. Treading on thin ice over deep water; rising early, keeping parents warm and cool. Like orchids in fragrance; like pines in flourishing. Rivers flow without ceasing; deep pools reflect clearly. In demeanor, appear thoughtful; in speech, be calm and steady. Be sincere and fine at the start; be careful and proper at the end. The foundation of glory and enterprise; its basis is vast beyond measure. When learning excels, enter government service; hold office and join in governance. Preserve like the sweet pear tree; depart and be praised even more. Joy differs between noble and humble; rites distinguish high and low. Above harmonious, below respectful; husband leads, wife follows. Outside, receive the tutor's instruction; inside, follow the mother's example. All the aunts, uncles, and elders; treat nephews and nieces as your own children. Brothers share deep bonds; of one breath, connected branches. In friendship, share commitments; polish and admonish each other. Benevolence, compassion, and sympathy; never depart from these, even in haste. Integrity, righteousness, modesty, and deference; never diminish these, even in hardship. When nature is calm, emotions are at ease; when the heart stirs, the spirit tires. Hold to truth and your will is full; chase things and your purpose shifts. Firmly maintain refined conduct; good rank will come of itself. The great cities of China; the two capitals, East and West. Backed by Mang, facing Luo; floating on the Wei, set upon the Jing. Palaces rise in lush splendor; towers and pavilions soar startlingly. Paintings depict birds and beasts; colors portray immortals and spirits. Side chambers open beside; curtained halls face the pillars. Banquets are spread with mats; drums, zithers, and reed organs play. Ascending the steps to the throne; caps turn like revolving stars. Right passage to the inner quarters; left leads to the Hall of Light. Classics and canons are gathered; talented scholars are assembled. Du Cao's drafts, Zhong's clerical script; lacquered writings, wall sutras. Officials arrayed: generals and ministers; flanking the lanes, ministers by the scholar trees. Households enfeoffed in eight counties; families supplied with a thousand soldiers. Tall caps accompany the imperial chariot; carriages surge, tassels flutter. Hereditary wealth and luxury; carriages sleek, horses light. Meritorious deeds richly recorded; inscribed on steles and carved in stone. Pan Xi and Yi Yin; aiding their times, the Grand Steward. Dwelling at Qufu; who but Dan could have built it? Duke Huan united and corrected; aiding the weak, supporting the faltering. Qi turned back the Han and the Hui; Yue's persuasion moved King Wu Ding. Outstanding talents served diligently; many scholars brought genuine peace. Jin and Chu competed for supremacy; Zhao and Wei were hemmed in. Borrowing a road to destroy Guo; treading the soil at the covenant assembly. He Zun upheld the law; Han's legacy burdened by harsh punishment. Qi Jian, Po, and Mu; their military use was the most brilliant. Proclaiming might across the desert; fame racing through painted history. The nine provinces bear Yu's traces; a hundred commanderies under Qin's union. The sacred peak Mount Tai; the altar of Zen at Cloud Pavilion. Wild Goose Gate, the Purple Pass; Cock Field, the Red Walls. Kunming Pool, Jieshi Rock; the Great Wilds, Dongting Lake. Vast and far, stretching endlessly; cliffs and peaks, dark and deep. Governance is rooted in agriculture; attend to planting and harvesting. Begin plowing the southern fields; I plant millet and grain. When taxes are ripe, offer the new harvest; encourage with rewards, demote and promote. Mencius valued simplicity; Shi Yu held to uprightness. Strive for the Mean; be diligent, humble, and careful. Listen to sounds, examine principles; observe appearance, discern character. Bequeath excellent plans; encourage earnest cultivation. Examine yourself with admonition; favor and excess lead to extremes. Disgrace and humiliation draw near shame; the forest and marsh are fortunate retreats. The two Shu perceived the moment; who compelled them to resign? Dwell in solitude, abide in leisure; in silence and stillness. Seek the ancients, explore their words; scatter worries, wander carefree. Joyful melodies dispel sorrow; sorrows depart, happiness beckons. Lotus channels, water lilies; gardens overgrown, tendrils reaching. Loquats green in late season; parasol trees wither early. Old roots hidden in shadow; fallen leaves drift and sway. The great fish swims alone; soaring, brushing the crimson sky. Lost in reading at the market; eyes fixed on the book satchel. Easy and light are what we fear; walls have ears. Prepare meals and serve food; suit the palate, fill the belly. When sated, cook and slaughter; when hungry, even dregs and husks suffice. Relatives and old friends; old and young get different fare. Concubines spin and weave; attendants serve in chambers. Round fans of fine silk; silver candles gleaming bright. Daytime sleep, evening slumber; blue bamboo mats, ivory beds. String songs and wine banquets; raising cups and lifting goblets. Clapping hands and stamping feet; in joy and ease and health. Legitimate heirs carry on the line; sacrificial rites of winter and autumn. Kowtow and bow again; with awe, fear, and trepidation. Letters and documents should be concise; replies should be thorough. When the body is dirty, think of bathing; when hot, wish for coolness. Donkeys, mules, calves, and bulls; startled, they leap and prance. Execute and behead thieves and bandits; capture and seize rebels and fugitives. Bu Yi's archery, Liao Wan's ball play; Ji Kang's zither, Ruan Ji's whistling. Tian's brush, Lun's paper; Jun's ingenuity, Ren's fishing. Release disputes for common benefit; all are fine and wonderful. Mao Qiang and Xi Shi's beauty; artful frowns, lovely smiles. Years fly like arrows, always pressing; the sun's glow shines brightly. The celestial armillary sphere revolves; the dark moon's phases cycle in light. Point to the firewood to prolong blessings; forever peaceful, auspicious, and good. Measured steps, leading the way; looking up and down in the corridors of state. Bound sashes, dignified and solemn; lingering, gazing afar. Lonely and ignorant, few in learning; foolish and benighted, subject to ridicule. These are the grammatical particles: yan, zai, hu, ye.

Cold comes, heat goes; autumn harvests, winter stores. Intercalary months complete the year; musical pitches harmonize with yang. Clouds rise to bring rain; dew condenses into frost. Gold is born in beautiful waters; jade comes from Kungang. The sword called Juque; the pearl known as Night-Shining. Precious fruits: plums and crabapples; important vegetables: mustard and ginger. The sea is salty, rivers are fresh; fish dive, birds soar. Dragon Master, Fire Emperor; Bird Official, Human Sovereign. They began creating writing; then came clothing and garments. Yielding the throne, ceding the state: Yu and Tang of the line of Tao. Comforting the people, punishing the guilty: King Fa of Zhou, King Tang of Yin. Sitting in court, inquiring of the Way; ruling effortlessly, bringing order. Lovingly nurturing the common people; subjects submitting, even the Rong and Qiang. Far and near, one body; all guests return to the king. Phoenixes sing in the bamboo; white colts graze in the meadow. Transformation covers the grasses and trees; its blessings reach all directions. This body and its hair come from the four elements and five constants. Respectfully cherish your upbringing; dare not damage or injure. Women admire chastity and purity; men emulate talent and virtue. Know your faults and always correct them; gain ability and never forget it. Do not speak of others' shortcomings; do not rely on your own strengths. Trustworthiness should be verifiable; one's capacity is hard to measure. Mo Zi grieved over dyed silk; the Odes praised the lambskin. Emulate virtuous conduct; strive to be a sage in thought. Build virtue, establish a name; keep form upright, appearance correct. An empty valley carries sound; a vacant hall echoes. Disaster comes from accumulated evil; fortune follows from doing good. A foot of jade is not the treasure; an inch of time is what to compete for. Serve your father, serve your lord, with strictness and respect. In filial piety, exhaust your strength; in loyalty, devote your life. Treading on thin ice over deep water; rising early, keeping parents warm and cool. Like orchids in fragrance; like pines in flourishing. Rivers flow without ceasing; deep pools reflect clearly. In demeanor, appear thoughtful; in speech, be calm and steady. Be sincere and fine at the start; be careful and proper at the end. The foundation of glory and enterprise; its basis is vast beyond measure. When learning excels, enter government service; hold office and join in governance. Preserve like the sweet pear tree; depart and be praised even more. Joy differs between noble and humble; rites distinguish high and low. Above harmonious, below respectful; husband leads, wife follows. Outside, receive the tutor's instruction; inside, follow the mother's example. All the aunts, uncles, and elders; treat nephews and nieces as your own children. Brothers share deep bonds; of one breath, connected branches. In friendship, share commitments; polish and admonish each other. Benevolence, compassion, and sympathy; never depart from these, even in haste. Integrity, righteousness, modesty, and deference; never diminish these, even in hardship. When nature is calm, emotions are at ease; when the heart stirs, the spirit tires. Hold to truth and your will is full; chase things and your purpose shifts. Firmly maintain refined conduct; good rank will come of itself. The great cities of China; the two capitals, East and West. Backed by Mang, facing Luo; floating on the Wei, set upon the Jing. Palaces rise in lush splendor; towers and pavilions soar startlingly. Paintings depict birds and beasts; colors portray immortals and spirits. Side chambers open beside; curtained halls face the pillars. Banquets are spread with mats; drums, zithers, and reed organs play. Ascending the steps to the throne; caps turn like revolving stars. Right passage to the inner quarters; left leads to the Hall of Light. Classics and canons are gathered; talented scholars are assembled. Du Cao's drafts, Zhong's clerical script; lacquered writings, wall sutras. Officials arrayed: generals and ministers; flanking the lanes, ministers by the scholar trees. Households enfeoffed in eight counties; families supplied with a thousand soldiers. Tall caps accompany the imperial chariot; carriages surge, tassels flutter. Hereditary wealth and luxury; carriages sleek, horses light. Meritorious deeds richly recorded; inscribed on steles and carved in stone. Pan Xi and Yi Yin; aiding their times, the Grand Steward. Dwelling at Qufu; who but Dan could have built it? Duke Huan united and corrected; aiding the weak, supporting the faltering. Qi turned back the Han and the Hui; Yue's persuasion moved King Wu Ding. Outstanding talents served diligently; many scholars brought genuine peace. Jin and Chu competed for supremacy; Zhao and Wei were hemmed in. Borrowing a road to destroy Guo; treading the soil at the covenant assembly. He Zun upheld the law; Han's legacy burdened by harsh punishment. Qi Jian, Po, and Mu; their military use was the most brilliant. Proclaiming might across the desert; fame racing through painted history. The nine provinces bear Yu's traces; a hundred commanderies under Qin's union. The sacred peak Mount Tai; the altar of Zen at Cloud Pavilion. Wild Goose Gate, the Purple Pass; Cock Field, the Red Walls. Kunming Pool, Jieshi Rock; the Great Wilds, Dongting Lake. Vast and far, stretching endlessly; cliffs and peaks, dark and deep. Governance is rooted in agriculture; attend to planting and harvesting. Begin plowing the southern fields; I plant millet and grain. When taxes are ripe, offer the new harvest; encourage with rewards, demote and promote. Mencius valued simplicity; Shi Yu held to uprightness. Strive for the Mean; be diligent, humble, and careful. Listen to sounds, examine principles; observe appearance, discern character. Bequeath excellent plans; encourage earnest cultivation. Examine yourself with admonition; favor and excess lead to extremes. Disgrace and humiliation draw near shame; the forest and marsh are fortunate retreats. The two Shu perceived the moment; who compelled them to resign? Dwell in solitude, abide in leisure; in silence and stillness. Seek the ancients, explore their words; scatter worries, wander carefree. Joyful melodies dispel sorrow; sorrows depart, happiness beckons. Lotus channels, water lilies; gardens overgrown, tendrils reaching. Loquats green in late season; parasol trees wither early. Old roots hidden in shadow; fallen leaves drift and sway. The great fish swims alone; soaring, brushing the crimson sky. Lost in reading at the market; eyes fixed on the book satchel. Easy and light are what we fear; walls have ears. Prepare meals and serve food; suit the palate, fill the belly. When sated, cook and slaughter; when hungry, even dregs and husks suffice. Relatives and old friends; old and young get different fare. Concubines spin and weave; attendants serve in chambers. Round fans of fine silk; silver candles gleaming bright. Daytime sleep, evening slumber; blue bamboo mats, ivory beds. String songs and wine banquets; raising cups and lifting goblets. Clapping hands and stamping feet; in joy and ease and health. Legitimate heirs carry on the line; sacrificial rites of winter and autumn. Kowtow and bow again; with awe, fear, and trepidation. Letters and documents should be concise; replies should be thorough. When the body is dirty, think of bathing; when hot, wish for coolness. Donkeys, mules, calves, and bulls; startled, they leap and prance. Execute and behead thieves and bandits; capture and seize rebels and fugitives. Bu Yi's archery, Liao Wan's ball play; Ji Kang's zither, Ruan Ji's whistling. Tian's brush, Lun's paper; Jun's ingenuity, Ren's fishing. Release disputes for common benefit; all are fine and wonderful. Mao Qiang and Xi Shi's beauty; artful frowns, lovely smiles. Years fly like arrows, always pressing; the sun's glow shines brightly. The celestial armillary sphere revolves; the dark moon's phases cycle in light. Point to the firewood to prolong blessings; forever peaceful, auspicious, and good. Measured steps, leading the way; looking up and down in the corridors of state. Bound sashes, dignified and solemn; lingering, gazing afar. Lonely and ignorant, few in learning; foolish and benighted, subject to ridicule. These are the grammatical particles: yan, zai, hu, ye.

Phoenixes sing in the bamboo; white colts graze in the meadow. Transformation covers the grasses and trees; its blessings reach all directions. This body and its hair come from the four elements and five constants. Respectfully cherish your upbringing; dare not damage or injure. Women admire chastity and purity; men emulate talent and virtue. Know your faults and always correct them; gain ability and never forget it. Do not speak of others' shortcomings; do not rely on your own strengths. Trustworthiness should be verifiable; one's capacity is hard to measure. Mo Zi grieved over dyed silk; the Odes praised the lambskin. Emulate virtuous conduct; strive to be a sage in thought. Build virtue, establish a name; keep form upright, appearance correct. An empty valley carries sound; a vacant hall echoes. Disaster comes from accumulated evil; fortune follows from doing good. A foot of jade is not the treasure; an inch of time is what to compete for. Serve your father, serve your lord, with strictness and respect. In filial piety, exhaust your strength; in loyalty, devote your life. Treading on thin ice over deep water; rising early, keeping parents warm and cool. Like orchids in fragrance; like pines in flourishing. Rivers flow without ceasing; deep pools reflect clearly. In demeanor, appear thoughtful; in speech, be calm and steady. Be sincere and fine at the start; be careful and proper at the end. The foundation of glory and enterprise; its basis is vast beyond measure. When learning excels, enter government service; hold office and join in governance. Preserve like the sweet pear tree; depart and be praised even more. Joy differs between noble and humble; rites distinguish high and low. Above harmonious, below respectful; husband leads, wife follows. Outside, receive the tutor's instruction; inside, follow the mother's example. All the aunts, uncles, and elders; treat nephews and nieces as your own children. Brothers share deep bonds; of one breath, connected branches. In friendship, share commitments; polish and admonish each other. Benevolence, compassion, and sympathy; never depart from these, even in haste. Integrity, righteousness, modesty, and deference; never diminish these, even in hardship. When nature is calm, emotions are at ease; when the heart stirs, the spirit tires. Backed by Mang, facing Luo; floating on the Wei, set upon the Jing. Palaces rise in lush splendor; towers and pavilions soar startlingly. Banquets are spread with mats; drums, zithers, and reed organs play. Ascending the steps to the throne; caps turn like revolving stars. Right passage to the inner quarters; left leads to the Hall of Light. Classics and canons are gathered; talented scholars are assembled. Du Cao's drafts, Zhong's clerical script; lacquered writings, wall sutras. Officials arrayed: generals and ministers; flanking the lanes, ministers by the scholar trees. Households enfeoffed in eight counties; families supplied with a thousand soldiers. Tall caps accompany the imperial chariot; carriages surge, tassels flutter. Wild Goose Gate, the Purple Pass; Cock Field, the Red Walls. Kunming Pool, Jieshi Rock; the Great Wilds, Dongting Lake. Vast and far, stretching endlessly; cliffs and peaks, dark and deep. Governance is rooted in agriculture; attend to planting and harvesting. Begin plowing the southern fields; I plant millet and grain. When taxes are ripe, offer the new harvest; encourage with rewards, demote and promote. Mencius valued simplicity; Shi Yu held to uprightness. Strive for the Mean; be diligent, humble, and careful. Listen to sounds, examine principles; observe appearance, discern character. Bequeath excellent plans; encourage earnest cultivation. Examine yourself with admonition; favor and excess lead to extremes. Disgrace and humiliation draw near shame; the forest and marsh are fortunate retreats. The two Shu perceived the moment; who compelled them to resign? Dwell in solitude, abide in leisure; in silence and stillness. Seek the ancients, explore their words; scatter worries, wander carefree. Joyful melodies dispel sorrow; sorrows depart, happiness beckons. Lotus channels, water lilies; gardens overgrown, tendrils reaching. Loquats green in late season; parasol trees wither early. Old roots hidden in shadow; fallen leaves drift and sway. The great fish swims alone; soaring, brushing the crimson sky. Lost in reading at the market; eyes fixed on the book satchel. Easy and light are what we fear; walls have ears. Prepare meals and serve food; suit the palate, fill the belly. When sated, cook and slaughter; when hungry, even dregs and husks suffice. Relatives and old friends; old and young get different fare. Concubines spin and weave; attendants serve in chambers. Round fans of fine silk; silver candles gleaming bright. Daytime sleep, evening slumber; blue bamboo mats, ivory beds. String songs and wine banquets; raising cups and lifting goblets. Clapping hands and stamping feet; in joy and ease and health. Legitimate heirs carry on the line; sacrificial rites of winter and autumn. Kowtow and bow again; with awe, fear, and trepidation. Letters and documents should be concise; replies should be thorough. When the body is dirty, think of bathing; when hot, wish for coolness. Donkeys, mules, calves, and bulls; startled, they leap and prance. Execute and behead thieves and bandits; capture and seize rebels and fugitives. Bu Yi's archery, Liao Wan's ball play; Ji Kang's zither, Ruan Ji's whistling. Tian's brush, Lun's paper; Jun's ingenuity, Ren's fishing. Release disputes for common benefit; all are fine and wonderful. Mao Qiang and Xi Shi's beauty; artful frowns, lovely smiles. Years fly like arrows, always pressing; the sun's glow shines brightly. The celestial armillary sphere revolves; the dark moon's phases cycle in light. Point to the firewood to prolong blessings; forever peaceful, auspicious, and good. Measured steps, leading the way; looking up and down in the corridors of state. Bound sashes, dignified and solemn; lingering, gazing afar. Lonely and ignorant, few in learning; foolish and benighted, subject to ridicule. These are the grammatical particles: yan, zai, hu, ye.

Prepare meals and serve food; suit the palate, fill the belly. When sated, cook and slaughter; when hungry, even dregs and husks suffice. Relatives and old friends; old and young get different fare. Concubines spin and weave; attendants serve in chambers. Round fans of fine silk; silver candles gleaming bright. Daytime sleep, evening slumber; blue bamboo mats, ivory beds. String songs and wine banquets; raising cups and lifting goblets. Clapping hands and stamping feet; in joy and ease and health. Legitimate heirs carry on the line; sacrificial rites of winter and autumn. Kowtow and bow again; with awe, fear, and trepidation. Letters and documents should be concise; replies should be thorough. When the body is dirty, think of bathing; when hot, wish for coolness. Donkeys, mules, calves, and bulls; startled, they leap and prance. Execute and behead thieves and bandits; capture and seize rebels and fugitives. Bu Yi's archery, Liao Wan's ball play; Ji Kang's zither, Ruan Ji's whistling. Tian's brush, Lun's paper; Jun's ingenuity, Ren's fishing. Release disputes for common benefit; all are fine and wonderful. Mao Qiang and Xi Shi's beauty; artful frowns, lovely smiles. Years fly like arrows, always pressing; the sun's glow shines brightly. The celestial armillary sphere revolves; the dark moon's phases cycle in light. Point to the firewood to prolong blessings; forever peaceful, auspicious, and good. Measured steps, leading the way; looking up and down in the corridors of state. Bound sashes, dignified and solemn; lingering, gazing afar. Lonely and ignorant, few in learning; foolish and benighted, subject to ridicule. These are the grammatical particles: yan, zai, hu, ye.
